name: Freedom Whale Watch
summary: Freedom Whale Watch runs a full-day humpback whale watching cruise from Urangan in Hervey Bay on Freedom III, a 58ft catamaran with three viewing levels. The cruise runs in the July to October whale season, with morning tea, a buffet lunch and afternoon tea on board. Outside the season the boat can be hired for private charters.
standouts: Certified through Ecotourism Australia's ECO and ROC certification programs
Listed in Queensland's Best Experiences of 2025
Licensed for up to 48 guests on the Freedom III catamaran
Free bus transfers from Hervey Bay accommodation on direct bookings

contact.address: Great Sandy Straits Marina, Buccaneer Drive, Urangan, Hervey Bay QLD 4655

trips.title: Freedom Whale Watch Cruise
trips.summary: A full-day cruise on Freedom III from the Great Sandy Straits Marina into Platypus Bay, off K'gari (Fraser Island), to watch humpback whales. Morning tea, a buffet lunch and afternoon tea are served on board, and the crew gives commentary along the way. There is one departure a day, with up to 48 guests, during the whale season.
highlights: Departs 9:30am and returns to the marina around 3:30pm
Morning tea, buffet lunch and afternoon tea included
Return bus transfers from Hervey Bay accommodation on direct bookings
Three viewing levels, an air-conditioned saloon, three toilets and a water-level platform
trips.departsFrom: Great Sandy Straits Marina, Buccaneer Drive, Urangan, Hervey Bay
includes: Return bus transfers from Hervey Bay accommodation (direct bookings only)
Morning tea: tea, coffee, hot chocolate and home-baked treats
Buffet lunch, usually hot chicken, cold deli meats, three salads and fresh bread
Afternoon tea, usually a selection of cheese with crackers and fruit
bring: Camera with a wrist or neck strap
Proof of age, or a valid concession or student card, if booked on a discounted ticket
trips.requirements: Not suitable for wheelchairs, walking frames, pushchairs or prams. All guests need enough unassisted mobility to manage 5 steps with a handrail. Infants aged 0 to 3 are not recommended, and the operator asks to be contacted to book an infant. Children are aged 4 to 17, with a limit of three children per responsible adult. Guests must tell the operator at booking about any physical, sensory, cognitive or food allergy needs.

trips.checkNotes: No adult or child prices appear anywhere on the operator's site; they are only in the booking system, which was not opened. So prices is empty and priceFrom is null. The only dollar figures on the site for this trip are the family group child price ('$75 or less', held in the offer above) and the companion card price (operator-level offers). Season status: the home page says 'We are no longer taking any booking for the 2026 whale watching season', and no 2027 dates are given, so confirm whether the cruise is open for booking. Season text varies: the About page says July to October every year, the Terms page says the best period is late July to late September, and the 2026 return-cruise dates run 11 July to 29 September 2026. Times: the itinerary on the cruise page gives 8:30am courtesy transfers, 9:30am departure and 3:30pm return, while the home page says board at 9:10am and return at 3:30pm earliest; the itinerary says times may vary with weather. Duration '6 hours minimum' is from the competitor comparison page and matches 9:30am to 3:30pm. The site calls this trip Freedom Whale Watch Cruise, Freedom Premium Whale Watch Cruise and Freedom Whale Odyssey Cruise; the title follows the menu item 'Book the Freedom Whale Watch Cruise'. Vessel length is 60 feet on the home and cruise pages but 58ft (17.7m) on the About, charter and comparison text; used 58ft. Maximum 48 guests comes from the About page (licensed for up to 48 in the Bay area) and the Sustainability page. The Terms page says whale sightings cannot be guaranteed and offers a free return cruise in the 2026 season if no whale is sighted, while the competitor page says 'Guaranteed close encounters'; no sighting guarantee is repeated here. Review counts and rating comparisons on the site were left out. The bring list is from a 2014 blog post written under the previous owners; that post also says jackets can be borrowed, which was not repeated and should be confirmed. Bus transfers are for direct bookings only. The booking link on the site carries Google tracking parameters; the clean link is recorded.

trips.title: Private Charters
trips.summary: Freedom can be hired privately with skipper and crew for small weddings, birthdays, hen's and bucks parties, anniversaries, Christmas functions and corporate events. A charter can include swimming near Pelican Bank or the western beaches of K'gari, or a relaxed cruise through the Great Sandy Strait Marine Park. Hire is for a minimum of four hours, starting at $3000.
highlights: Private hire with skipper and crew
Swimming in the pool or calm waters near Pelican Bank or the western beaches of K'gari
Overnight charters for up to 10 guests within Hervey Bay waters

trips.checkNotes: Described only in a section on the home page, with a Book Now button and a menu link ('Private Charters, Affordable luxury') that both go to the same booking link; there is no separate charter page. The only price is the minimum 4-hour hire 'starting at $3000'; the site does not say what that covers, so treat it as a from price for the whole boat and confirm. Departure point is not stated for charters (the boat is berthed at the Great Sandy Straits Marina), so departsFrom is null. Season is unclear: the menu link title says October to July, the booking link name says October to June, and the About page says private charters run in summer from November until March (beach cruises, sunset cruises and Mary River trips). Peak season private whale watch tours are listed as a charter option with no details. The catering line reads 'BYO food and drink catering licenced bar and BYO food catering', which is ambiguous. 'Swimming in our pool' is not explained on the site. Maximum charter numbers are not stated; the About page says the vessel is licensed for up to 48 in the Bay area.

checkNotes: Main pages read (about 25 pages; guest reviews, accommodation and other-travel-links were not read; no bot check or block met). Legal operator name is Freedom Ecotours Pty Ltd (Mark and Andrea Cooper, owners); the trading name on the site is Freedom Whale Watch. Contact: the contact page gives Freecall 1300 388 688 and a mobile, 0448 773 668 (+61 448773668), for Andrea. Email andrea@freedomecotours.com.au is used throughout; the Terms page also shows andrea@freedomwhalewatch.com.au and info@freedomwhalewatching.com.au, so confirm which inbox is monitored. The privacy policy gives the business address as Berth 4A, Great Sandy Straits Marina, 17 Buccaneer Drive, Urangan; the contact page omits the berth. Only two sellable products exist on the site: the whale watch cruise and private charters, both linked to Rezdy (freedomwhalewatching.rezdy.com, not opened). Old gallery names and blog posts mention scuba diving, fishing charters and summer adventure cruises, but no current page sells them, so they are not included. Cancellation terms (Terms page): if the operator cancels, guests choose another date in the season or a refund; if the guest cancels, no refund within 24 hours of departure, a half refund between 24 and 48 hours and a full refund beyond 48 hours, in each case less agent commission. Operator-level claims left out of copy: review counts, 'only whale tour with a five star Google rating', competitor comparison table, the 'Guaranteed close encounters' line and the free return cruise offer. The booking links on the page have tracking parameters, which were removed. Not opened: Rezdy pages, Facebook, Instagram, Tripadvisor.
